after a review pass that upgrades `Speaker 1` to a real name.

a `{language}_subtitle.srt` for each language, plus a `{language}_transcript.docx` for

Retrieve the tag filters (also called tag groups) configured for your company, each with
the list of tag option IDs that belong to it. A tag filter groups related tag options under
a stable identifier — for example a `Score` filter groups score tags like `2-1`, while a

IDs returned here against the `ID` field of the tag options from
[List tag options](#tag/operation/listTagOptionsPublic) or the `tag_options` on a
[media item](#tag/operation/getMediaByIdPublic). For example, a tag option whose ID appears
under the `Score` filter is a score, not a team or shirt number.

- The `id` is a stable internal identifier. It is safe to map integrations against it; it is
  unaffected when the filter is renamed.
- A tag option may belong to several filters, so the same tag option ID can appear under
  more than one filter.
- A filter with no associated tag options returns an empty `tag_options` array.
- Hidden (internal) filters are never returned.
- Results are ordered by the filter's configured display position, then by ID.

Retrieve the players for your company. Supports pagination, search by name, lookup by
external ID, and filtering down to a single team.

## Looking up a player by external ID

`external_id` matches the identifier you assigned to the player in your own system,
the same way [Get a team by External ID](#tag/operation/listTeamsPublic) does for teams.
The match is exact and case sensitive, and only one `external_id` is accepted per request.

External IDs are not guaranteed to be unique within an organization, so the response is
an array and every match is returned. To look a player up by ScorePlay's internal
identifier instead, use [Get a player by ID](#tag/operation/getPlayerPublic).

## Filtering by team

Supply whichever team identifier you already hold. `team_id` is ScorePlay's internal
team ID, as returned by [Get a team by ID](#tag/operation/getTeamPublic).
`team_external_id` is the identifier you assigned to the team in your own system, the
same one [Get a team by External ID](#tag/operation/listTeamsPublic) accepts.
Both return the roster across every season the team is registered in.

`team_season_id` scopes the response to one team-season association, so use it when you
want a single season's roster rather than the full history.

## Notes
- Omitting all three team parameters returns every player in your organization, as before.
- Supplying more than one team parameter returns the union of their players, not the
  intersection.
- `external_id` narrows the result rather than widening it. Combined with a team parameter
  or with `query`, only the players matching every filter are returned.
- An `external_id` or team identifier that matches nothing returns an empty array (`[]`)
  with status `200`, not a `404`.
- `team_external_id` is not guaranteed to be unique within an organization, so it may
  resolve to several teams. The players of every match are returned.
- Team-season IDs are not returned by the Teams endpoints. Resolve them with
  [List team-season associations](#tag/operation/listTeamSeasonsPublic), or filter
  with `team_id` or `team_external_id` instead.

description.content:
Retrieve the teams for your company. Supply `external_id` to look up teams by the
identifier you assigned in your own system, instead of by ScorePlay's internal team ID
as [Get a team by ID](#tag/operation/getTeamPublic) requires. When `external_id` is
omitted, all teams for your organization are returned.

## Notes
- `external_id` is not guaranteed to be unique within an organization, so a lookup may
  return more than one team. Treat the response as a list, not a single team.
- An `external_id` with no match returns an empty array (`[]`) with status `200` — not
  a `404`.
- Association fields (`tag_options`, `sponsors`, `Seasons`) are `null` on this endpoint;
  they are not preloaded.

query.description: Filter teams by the partner-provided external identifier

response.name: Successfully retrieved teams. Returns an empty array when no team matches the supplied `external_id`.

Attach a batch of players to a team-season association, building that season's squad.
The call reports what it did per player rather than returning a bare success flag,
so a partially-correct batch tells you exactly which IDs were new, which were
already there, and which did not resolve.

`id` is the **team-season association ID**, the value
[List team-season associations](#tag/operation/listTeamSeasonsPublic) returns and
[List players](#tag/operation/listPlayersPublic) accepts as `team_season_id`. It is
not a team ID.

## Reading the response

Every ID you sent comes back in exactly one bucket:

| Bucket | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `attached` | Newly attached by this call (or, on a dry run, would be) |
| `already_present` | Already in this squad, left untouched |
| `not_found` | No player with that ID in your organization |

A player that exists in another organization is reported as `not_found`, never
attached, even if you hold its ID.

## Notes
- **Idempotent.** Re-posting the same squad reports everything as `already_present`
  and writes nothing.
- **`dry_run: true`** returns the identical report without writing, so a client-side
  spreadsheet can be validated before it is committed.
- **Duplicate and zero IDs are dropped** before the diff, so they never appear in
  the response.
- **Batches are capped at 500 IDs** and an oversized batch is rejected outright,
  not truncated.
- There is no matching read or delete endpoint. Read the squad with
  `GET /v1/players?team_season_id={id}`, which is paginated.
- This endpoint requires the `can_do_team_edit_player/team` permission. A key
  without it gets `401`, the same as an invalid key.

Perform advanced search for media content with comprehensive filtering options. This endpoint supports complex queries including date ranges, tag filtering, player/sponsor associations, and more.

## Search Capabilities
- Fuzzy text search on the file name (`name`) and on the description (`description`)
- Date range filtering
- Tag, player, and sponsor filtering (inclusive/exclusive)
- Media type filtering (photo/video)
- Event associations
- Pagination support

## Text search on name and description

`name` searches the file name, `description` searches the media description, and both
behave the same way:

- every word must match (AND), so `"final goal"` only returns media matching both words;
- small typos are tolerated: one wrong character per word, or up to two on longer words
  when `smart_filter` is set, so `"stadim"` still matches `"stadium"`;
- matching is on whole analysed words, not substrings, so `"stad"` does **not** match
  `"stadium"`.

Sending both `name` and `description` requires both to match. To match *either* of them,
or to combine free text with tag filters using OR, set `smart_filter: true`: a media is
then returned when it matches the tag filters **or** the name **or** the description,
numbers are matched exactly rather than fuzzily, and matches are scored with tags ranked
above name, and name above description. Scores only affect the ordering if you also send
`order_by: "relevance"`; results are otherwise sorted by upload date, newest first.

## Pagination

Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters, not by the body.
Defaults are page 1 and 100 results per page. The response echoes back `page`, `per_page`
and `total_pages`, next to `count`, the total number of matching media.

Paging by page number stops at the first 10,000 results: a request where `page` times
`per_page` goes past 10,000 fails. To read further, follow the cursor instead. Every
non-empty response carries a `next_cursor`; send it back as the `cursor` query parameter,
with the same body, to get the page that follows. Stop when a page comes back with fewer
than `per_page` media or without a `next_cursor`. A cursor only works with the `order_by` and `order_type` it was
issued with; change either and start again from page 1.

query.description: Page number for pagination (1-based)
Number of results per page. Defaults to 100 when omitted.

The `next_cursor` of the previous response. Returns the page that follows it, with no 10,000 result limit, and takes precedence over `page`. Must be sent with the same body, `order_by` and `order_type` as the request that returned it.

description.content:
Moves up to 500 media into another event (collection) and swaps their event-derived tags in one call. The previous event's tags (its tag options, team and season tags, and the teams' extra tag options) are removed, and the destination event's tags (tag options, team, season, players and sponsors) are added. All other tags, including existing player and sponsor tags, are kept.

The move runs asynchronously: the call returns `202` with an `operation_id`, which you poll with `GET /operation/{id}` until its `status` is `done` or `error`. Duplicate IDs are ignored. Media that have no files cannot be moved and end the operation in `error`.

Start uploading a file as a new version of an existing media. Use it to
save an edit made outside ScorePlay (Photoshop, Lightroom) back onto the
original: the media keeps its ID, name, tags, collection and access
restrictions, and the file is added to its `versions`.

1. Call this endpoint to create the version and get upload parameters
2. Upload the file parts with `PUT` to the returned `urls`, and keep the `ETag` header of each response
3. Call `POST /media/{id}/versions/{version_id}/complete` with the key, upload ID and part ETags

ScorePlay generates the previews of the new version (thumbnail,
compressed, video proxy) after the upload completes. For companies with
their own storage, the file is written to the customer bucket.

The file type must match the media type: a photo media takes any
non-video file (JPG, PNG, PSD, camera RAW), a video media only a video.

To cancel, call `POST /upload/abort` with the returned `key` and
`upload_id`. The version created by this call stays on the media without
a file.

Timecoded action logs within videos for highlight clips and sports analysis

Add action logs to videos for creating highlight clips and action analysis. This endpoint processes video timestamp data and creates action clips for sports analysis.

## Video Logs
- Creates action clips with precise timestamps
- Supports external ID matching for events
- Generates searchable action metadata

## Timing Modes

Each video log entry must use one of the following timing modes for the `log` object:

| Mode | Fields | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| **Offset single** | `offset` | Single point offset in seconds from the start of the video |
| **Offset range** | `start_offset` + `end_offset` | Offset range in seconds from the start of the video |
| **Unix single** | `action_timestamp` | Unix timestamp in seconds for a single action point. Optionally include `start_timestamp`/`end_timestamp` for clip boundaries |
| **Unix range** | `start_timestamp` + `end_timestamp` (no `action_timestamp`) | Unix timestamps in seconds defining a clip range |

The unix modes are converted to offsets using the start timecode of the
media's default (favourite) video version. If that timecode is wrong,
correct it with `timecode` on `PUT /media/{id}/details` and send the
logs again.

## Use Cases
- Sports highlight generation
- Video analysis and tagging
- Action timestamp recording

Retrieve the timecoded action logs attached to a video, in playback order.

## Timestamp units

The three timing fields do **not** share a unit, and this mirrors how they are stored:

| Field | Unit | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `timestamp` | **seconds** | Offset from the start of the video for the logged moment |
| `start_timestamp` | **milliseconds** | Offset from the start of the video for the clip in-point (`0` if the log has no range) |
| `end_timestamp` | **milliseconds** | Offset from the start of the video for the clip out-point (`0` if the log has no range) |

Whichever timing mode you used on `POST /video/logs`, the log is stored resolved to
offsets against the video, so unix timestamps sent at write time come back as offsets here.

## Preview assets

`thumbnail_url`, `sprite_url` and `playback_url` point at the log's preview assets.
They are produced asynchronously after the log is created, and again when its clip
range changes, so each field is omitted while the assets are not ready yet and on
logs that never had any generated. Use the URLs as returned.

## Pagination

Results are ordered by `timestamp`, then `id`, so paging is stable. `limit` defaults to
50 and is capped at 200; a larger value is clamped rather than rejected.

Search the video logs across every media of your organization, optionally narrowed to
one media or event (collection) and to the players, tag options and sponsors tagged on
the logs. To read the logs of a single media in playback order, `GET /media/{id}/logs`

## Filters

All filters are optional; an empty body `{}` returns every log of the organization.
Filters combine with AND, and so do the IDs inside each list: `"player_ids": [1, 2]`
only returns logs tagged with **both** players. IDs that do not exist, or that belong
to another organization, simply match nothing.

## Ordering

Results are grouped by media, by descending media ID unless `order_type` is `asc`.
Within a media, logs are always in playback order: by `start_timestamp`, then
`timestamp`, then `end_timestamp`, then log ID.

## Timestamp units

Same as `GET /media/{id}/logs`: `timestamp` is in **seconds**, `start_timestamp` and
`end_timestamp` are in **milliseconds**, all offsets from the start of the video.

## Pagination

Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters, not by the body.
Defaults are page 1 and 100 results per page; `per_page` is capped at 200, and a larger
value is clamped rather than rejected. The response echoes back the `page` and
`per_page` applied, next to `count`, the total number of matching logs.

A **hybrid agent** is a small ScorePlay service installed on a machine at your
premises (an office NAS, a stadium server, an OB truck). It watches local folders
and uploads new media to ScorePlay, so footage reaches your library without anyone
dragging files into a browser.

Three objects describe a hybrid setup:

| Object | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Site** | A physical location. A label grouping the agents installed there. | "Wembley - OB truck" |
| **Agent** | One installation on one host. Belongs to exactly one site. | "Truck ingest box" on host `ob-truck-ingest-01` |
| **Storage** | Where files live: an SMB share, an S3 bucket. Managed with the [Storages](#tag/storages) endpoints and shared by the whole organization. | The truck's NAS share |

An agent's **configuration** ties them together: it names the storages the agent
uses and the folders it watches. Storages are not attached to a site or an agent
directly; referencing a storage in an agent's configuration is what links them.

Create one site per location. A site can technically hold several agents, but
ScorePlay routes storage work to the most recent agent of a site, so run one agent
per site.

All site and agent endpoints require the `can_manage_storage` permission (part of
the default admin role) and only see your organization's sites, agents and
storages: another organization's IDs return `404`.

List the [sites](#tag/sites) of your organization. A site is a physical location
(an office, a stadium, an OB truck) that groups the hybrid agents installed there.

Requires the `can_manage_storage` permission on your API key.

## Notes
- Not paginated: an organization has a handful of sites.
- Deleted sites are not returned.

## Onboarding a machine end to end
1. **Create the storage** the agent will use, or find it with
   [List all storages](#tag/operation/listStorages). Note its `id`.
2. **Create a site**: `POST /agent/sites` with `{"label": "Wembley - OB truck"}`.
3. **Create the agent** on that site: `POST /agent/agents` with
   `{"site_id": "<site id>", "name": "Truck ingest box"}`. It starts `pending`.
4. **Set its configuration**: `PUT /agent/agents/{agent_id}/config` (example
   below). An agent cannot be installed without one.
5. **Issue the install command**: `POST /agent/agents/{agent_id}/install-token`
   with `{"scan_directory": "/mnt/nas/"}`, and run the returned
   `install_command` on the host. The command is a secret, valid 72 hours.
6. The agent registers and its `status` becomes `active`.

## The configuration
| Section | Role |
|---|---|
| `instance_config` | Agent-wide settings. `default_storage_id` (required) is the agent's main storage. |
| `cloud_configurations` | Named references to your storages, e.g. `"nas" → storage 6f1c…`. Only the storage ID and a prefix are stored; connection details and credentials come from the storage. |
| `watch_folders` | One entry per folder to monitor: which folder (relative to the install's `scan_directory`), which collection to file media into, which filters and tags to apply, and which `cloud_configurations` names to upload originals and proxies to. |
| `chunking_configs`, `config_tests` | Advanced. Leave empty unless ScorePlay set them up with you. |

into event 4821.

```json

  "instance_config": {
    "default_storage_id": "6f1c2a3b-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8"
  },
  "cloud_configurations": {
    "nas": {
      "cloud_provider": "smb",
      "storage_id": "6f1c2a3b-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8",
      "path_prefix": "ingest"
    }
  },
  "watch_folders": [
    {
      "path": "/Matchday/Camera1",
      "storage_id": "6f1c2a3b-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8",
      "scoreplay_collection_id": 4821,
      "generate_proxy": true,
      "keep_full_resolution": true,
      "full_res_cloud_configs": ["nas"],
      "allowed_extensions": [".mp4", ".mov", ".mxf"],
      "exclude_patterns": ["*.tmp", ".*"],
      "tags": ["matchday"]
    }
  ],
  "chunking_configs": {},
  "config_tests": [{ "name": "hasExe", "arg": "ffmpeg" }]
```

PUT replaces the whole configuration: GET it, edit it, PUT it back. The running
agent loads its configuration when it starts, so restart the agent service on the
host to apply the change.

Retrieve the live schedules of your organization. A live schedule books a recording
of a live source (a stream, a stream group, a pull receiver or an SRT caller) between
a `start` and an `end`, and files the result into a collection. The response is a
paginated envelope carrying `items` and a `total` count, not a bare array.

- `name` matches the schedule name as a case-insensitive substring.
- `start_date` and `end_date` both bound the schedule's `start` (Unix seconds).

- `status` matches the status stored by the ingest pipeline. Older schedules that
  predate it carry no stored status and never match this filter.
- Filters combine: supplying several returns the schedules matching all of them.

## Notes
- Without `order_by`, the newest schedules come first.

- A schedule ID belonging to another organization returns `404`, the same as one
  that doesn't exist.

The ScorePlay Media API lets you search, enrich, transform, and deliver
media assets programmatically — the same library that powers your apps,
websites, and partner integrations.

All requests authenticate with an `X-ScorePlay-Api-Key` header and are scoped
to your organization. Responses are JSON; media search returns three
quality tiers (photographer, compressed, thumbnail) plus dynamic image URLs.

Use the **Try it** panel on any endpoint to call the live API with your key,
or download the OpenAPI spec and a ready-to-import Postman collection from
the Downloads menu.
